subtitle: "Exploring Powerhouses, Speed Offenses, and All 479 Division I Team-Seasons"

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(jsonlite)
library(htmltools)

batting_2021 <- read_csv("batting2021.csv") |> mutate(Season = 2021L)
batting_2022 <- read_csv("batting2022.csv") |> mutate(Season = 2022L)
all_batting <- bind_rows(batting_2021, batting_2022)

team_seasons <- all_batting |>
  group_by(Team, Season) |>
  summarise(
    players = n(),
    star_idx = which.max(if_else(PA >= 50, OPS, -1)),
    star = Player[star_idx],
    star_ops = OPS[star_idx],
    star_hr = HR[star_idx],
    team_OBP = weighted.mean(OBP, PA),
    team_SLG = weighted.mean(SLG, PA),
    team_OPS = weighted.mean(OPS, PA),
    team_BA = sum(H) / sum(AB),
    total_R = sum(R),
    total_H = sum(H),
    total_HR = sum(HR),
    total_SB = sum(SB),
    total_CS = sum(CS),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(players >= 7)
```

One superstar can change an inning, but winning a conference or reaching Oklahoma City takes an entire batting order. Across **479 full NCAA Division I team-seasons** in 2021 and 2022 (programs with at least 7 qualifying hitters in the dataset), the typical college lineup posted an **.802 weighted OPS**—combining a **.363 On-Base Percentage (`OBP`)** with a **.439 Slugging Percentage (`SLG`)**.

Yet colleges built dangerous lineups using very different blueprints:

- **100-Homer Juggernauts:** Only four lineups cracked 100 home runs in a single season—**2021 Oklahoma (154)**, **2022 Oklahoma (149)**, **2022 Wichita State (111)**, and **2022 Arkansas (103)**.
- **Balanced Five-Tool Offenses:** Programs like **2022 Duke** (82 HRs, 74 SBs), **2022 UL Lafayette** (69 HRs, 80 SBs), and **2021 Miami (OH)** (74 HRs, 71 SBs) reached the national Top 15 by pairing over-the-fence power with relentless base stealing.
- **Track-Meet Pressure:** **Southeastern Louisiana** stole **142 bases in 2021** and **133 in 2022**—climbing to a **.912 team OPS** in 2022 despite hitting only 31 home runs—alongside speed-first contenders like **2022 Florida** (126 SBs) and **2022 McNeese** (128 SBs).

## Top 15 Single-Season Lineups (2021–2022)

Hover over any bar below to inspect the **15 strongest college offenses** of 2021 and 2022 ranked by plate-appearance-weighted `OPS`, including each lineup's top hitter. Back-to-back national champion **Oklahoma** holds the top two spots by more than 100 OPS points.

```{r}
top_teams <- team_seasons |>
  slice_max(order_by = team_OPS, n = 15) |>
  mutate(
    SeasonLabel = paste0(Season, " Season"),
    TeamSeason = paste0(Team, " ('", substr(as.character(Season), 3, 4), ")"),
    TeamSeason = fct_reorder(TeamSeason, team_OPS)
  )

p_teams <- top_teams |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = team_OPS,
    y = TeamSeason,
    fill = SeasonLabel,
    text = paste0(
      "<b>", Team, " (", Season, ")</b>",
      "<br>Weighted OPS: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_OPS),
      " (", sprintf("%.3f", team_OBP), " OBP / ", sprintf("%.3f", team_SLG), " SLG)",
      "<br>Team Batting Avg: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_BA),
      "<br>Runs: ", total_R, " | Home Runs: ", total_HR, " | Steals: ", total_SB,
      "<br>OPS Leader: ", star, " (", sprintf("%.3f", star_ops), " OPS, ", star_hr, " HR)"
    )
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("2021 Season" = "#1d4ed8", "2022 Season" = "#b91c1c"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.85, 1.32)) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 15 NCAA D1 Softball Offenses by Weighted OPS",
    x = "Lineup Weighted OPS (On-Base + Slugging)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p_teams, tooltip = "text", height = 540) |>
  layout(
    title = list(font = list(size = 15), x = 0, xref = "paper"),
    margin = list(t = 60, b = 110, l = 180, r = 30),
    xaxis = list(automargin = TRUE, title = list(standoff = 14)),
    yaxis = list(automargin = TRUE),
    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0.5,
      xanchor = "center",
      y = -0.22
    )
  )
```

## Offensive Blueprints: Getting on Base vs. Hitting for Power

How does your favorite college stack up against the rest of Division I? The interactive scatter plot below maps **all 479 team-seasons** by **On-Base Percentage (`OBP`)** on the horizontal axis and **Slugging Percentage (`SLG`)** on the vertical axis, with **dot size showing team home runs** and dashed lines marking the national averages (`.363 OBP`, `.439 SLG`). Hover over any dot to inspect a lineup, drag to zoom into crowded clusters, or click **2021** or **2022** in the legend to isolate one season.

```{r}
p_blueprint <- team_seasons |>
  mutate(SeasonLabel = paste0(Season, " Season")) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = team_OBP,
    y = team_SLG,
    color = SeasonLabel,
    size = total_HR,
    text = paste0(
      "<b>", Team, " (", Season, ")</b>",
      "<br>Weighted OPS: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_OPS),
      "<br>OBP: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_OBP), " | SLG: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_SLG),
      " | BA: ", sprintf("%.3f", team_BA),
      "<br>Home Runs: ", total_HR, " | Stolen Bases: ", total_SB, " | Runs: ", total_R,
      "<br>Top Hitter: ", star, " (", sprintf("%.3f", star_ops), " OPS)"
    )
  )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(team_seasons$team_OBP), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(team_seasons$team_SLG), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray55") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.72) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("2021 Season" = "#1d4ed8", "2022 Season" = "#b91c1c"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.6, 7.5), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "All 479 D1 Lineups: Team OBP vs. SLG (Dot Size = HRs)",
    x = "Team On-Base Percentage (Weighted OBP)",
    y = "Team Slugging Percentage (Weighted SLG)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p_blueprint, tooltip = "text", height = 510) |>
  layout(
    title = list(font = list(size = 15), x = 0, xref = "paper"),
    margin = list(t = 60, b = 115, l = 80, r = 30),
    xaxis = list(automargin = TRUE, title = list(standoff = 14)),
    yaxis = list(automargin = TRUE, title = list(standoff = 12)),
    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0.5,
      xanchor = "center",
      y = -0.26
    )
  )
```

## Interactive All-D1 Lineup Leaderboard

Use the filters below to explore all **479 Division I team-seasons**—switch between **2021** and **2022**, re-rank teams by **OPS**, **Home Runs**, **Stolen Bases**, **Batting Average**, or **Runs**, or type a school or star player's name to compare lineups instantly.

```{r}
leaderboard_rows <- team_seasons |>
  transmute(
    Team,
    Season,
    BA = round(team_BA, 3),
    OBP = round(team_OBP, 3),
    SLG = round(team_SLG, 3),
    OPS = round(team_OPS, 3),
    R = total_R,
    HR = total_HR,
    SB = total_SB,
    Star = star,
    StarOPS = round(star_ops, 3)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(OPS))

lineup_json <- toJSON(leaderboard_rows, dataframe = "rows", auto_unbox = TRUE)

tagList(
  tags$div(
    class = "player-explorer-controls",
    tags$div(
      class = "player-control-group",
      tags$label(`for` = "lu-season", "Season"),
      tags$select(
        id = "lu-season",
        tags$option(value = "all", "Both Seasons (2021 & 2022)"),
        tags$option(value = "2021", "2021 Season Only"),
        tags$option(value = "2022", "2022 Season Only")
      )
    ),
    tags$div(
      class = "player-control-group",
      tags$label(`for` = "lu-sort", "Rank Lineups By"),
      tags$select(
        id = "lu-sort",
        tags$option(value = "OPS", "Weighted OPS (Overall)"),
        tags$option(value = "HR", "Home Runs (Power)"),
        tags$option(value = "SB", "Stolen Bases (Speed)"),
        tags$option(value = "BA", "Team Batting Average (Contact)"),
        tags$option(value = "R", "Total Runs Scored")
      )
    ),
    tags$div(
      class = "player-control-group",
      tags$label(`for` = "lu-search", "Search College or Star Hitter"),
      tags$input(
        id = "lu-search",
        type = "search",
        placeholder = "e.g. Oklahoma, Duke, Florida, Jocelyn Alo..."
      )
    )
  ),
  tags$div(id = "lu-count", class = "player-match-count"),
  tags$div(
    class = "player-card",
    tags$div(
      class = "player-stats-table-wrap",
      tags$table(
        class = "player-stats-table",
        tags$thead(
          tags$tr(
            tags$th("#"),
            tags$th("College"),
            tags$th("Season"),
            tags$th("BA"),
            tags$th("OBP"),
            tags$th("SLG"),
            tags$th("OPS"),
            tags$th("Runs"),
            tags$th("HR"),
            tags$th("SB"),
            tags$th("OPS Leader")
          )
        ),
        tags$tbody(id = "lu-tbody")
      )
    )
  ),
  tags$script(id = "lu-data", type = "application/json", HTML(lineup_json)),
  tags$script(HTML("
    (function() {
      const rows = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('lu-data').textContent);
      const seasonSel = document.getElementById('lu-season');
      const sortSel = document.getElementById('lu-sort');
      const searchIn = document.getElementById('lu-search');
      const countEl = document.getElementById('lu-count');
      const tbody = document.getElementById('lu-tbody');

      function fmt3(x) { return Number(x).toFixed(3); }

      function render() {
        const yr = seasonSel.value;
        const metric = sortSel.value;
        const q = searchIn.value.trim().toLowerCase();

        let list = rows.filter(r => {
          if (yr !== 'all' && String(r.Season) !== yr) return false;
          if (!q) return true;
          return (r.Team + ' ' + r.Star + ' ' + r.Season).toLowerCase().includes(q);
        });

        list.sort((a, b) => (b[metric] - a[metric]) || (b.OPS - a.OPS));

        const totalMatched = list.length;
        const shown = q ? list : list.slice(0, 50);

        countEl.textContent = q
          ? `Showing ${shown.length} matching lineup${shown.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`
          : `Showing top ${shown.length} of ${totalMatched} D1 team-seasons (type a school above to see any team)`;

        tbody.innerHTML = shown.map((r, idx) => {
          return `<tr>
            <td>${idx + 1}</td>
            <td style='text-align:left;'><strong>${r.Team}</strong></td>
            <td>${r.Season}</td>
            <td>${fmt3(r.BA)}</td>
            <td>${fmt3(r.OBP)}</td>
            <td>${fmt3(r.SLG)}</td>
            <td><strong>${fmt3(r.OPS)}</strong></td>
            <td>${r.R}</td>
            <td>${r.HR}</td>
            <td>${r.SB}</td>
            <td style='text-align:left;'>${r.Star} (${fmt3(r.StarOPS)})</td>
          </tr>`;
        }).join('');
      }

      seasonSel.addEventListener('change', render);
      sortSel.addEventListener('change', render);
      searchIn.addEventListener('input', render);
      render();
    })();
  "))
)
```
